title: Leylah Fernandez dominates Mirra Andreeva in Canadian Open upset
content:
TORONTO — Leylah Fernandez’s run at the Canadian Open isn’t done yet.

The Canadian trounced Mirra Andreeva, the world No. 5 and French Open champion, in straight sets 6-1, 6-4, on Friday afternoon to advance to the round of 16. After losing in the first round a year ago in Montreal, her birthplace, Fernandez has now matched her best result at the Canadian Open.

Fernandez started fast against Andreeva. After both players exchanged service holds, Fernandez rattled off five consecutive games to take the opening set in 31 minutes. The 23-year-old was 13 of 13 on first-serve points, controlling the rallies while Andreeva piled up unforced errors. On set point, Fernandez served up the T, and Andreeva blasted a forehand long, giving Fernandez the set. She fist-pumped to her box as the Canadian supporters inside Sobeys Stadium roared in approval.

Andreeva exited the court to gather herself. When she returned, the Fernandez domination continued. She broke Andreeva to start the second set, as the No. 5 seed’s serve continued to falter. Not only was Fernandez hitting her groundstrokes deep, but she was also mixing up her shots. In the third game of the second set, Fernandez connected on a forehand return down the line for the winner. Then she showcased a nifty drop shot, bringing Andreeva forward for a return attempt that resulted in another unforced error. Fernandez took a commanding double-break lead, not giving anything to Andreeva.

On the second chance to serve for the match, Fernandez didn’t squander the opportunity. With the match hers, she screamed to her box as the fans gave her a standing ovation. She waved and blew kisses to the crowd, beaming with joy for her biggest match win of the year.

Before this week, it had been a lackluster 2026 for Fernandez. She’s won just 14 WTA Tour matches this year, losing in the first round of all three Grand Slams. Her best result at a WTA 1000 was reaching the Madrid quarterfinal. It was at Madrid where Andreeva beat Fernandez in a close match 7-6 (1), 6-3, showcasing the Canadian’s potential against top-ranked opponents. But entering Friday, Fernandez was 0-4 against top-10 players, her most recent loss to fellow Canadian Victoria Mboko at Strasbourg.

That changed with her rout of Andreeva. The last time Fernandez reached the round of 16 at the Canadian Open came in 2023 in Montreal. Now, as the lone Canadian in the singles events for both ATP and WTA 1000 tournaments in Canada, Fernandez is chasing a career-best result in her home country. She will face the winner of four-time Slam champion Naomi Osaka and No. 20 seed Elise Mertens in the round of 16.
